record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.context_brief: Pair-breaking energy, order parameter, and Higgs interpretation
record.original_question: Beyond BCS theory and in experiments, what is the relation between the pair-breaking energy Epair, the order-parameter amplitude |Δ|, and the Higgs or amplitude branch of a pair-condensed Fermi gas? In particular, does Epair = 2|Δ| remain true at zero temperature in more accurate theories or measurements, and how should zero-wave-number order-parameter oscillation experiments be interpreted when their decay exponent, possible exponential damping, and lack of frequency softening near Tc do not match the simplest zero-temperature Higgs-oscillation picture?

evidence.quote: It would also be interesting to see whether property Epair = 2|∆| remains rigorously true at zero temperature in a theory more elaborate than BCS or in experiments.

The observations of reference [118] in a unitary Fermi gas atT ̸= 0 raise several questions: (i) the measured exponent α ≃ 1 ± 0.15 is very different from the theoretically predicted value (α = 1/2 at the unitary limit), (ii) it cannot be ruled out that the decay of the oscillation amplitude is in fact exponential, (iii) in contrast to the amplitude, the angular frequency of the oscillations shows no observable reduction asT approaches the transition temperature Tc

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional pair-condensed Fermi gas with two equally populated spin components and zero-range (s-wave) interactions, tunable through a Feshbach resonance and described, at the simplest level, by BCS mean-field theory. Within BCS theory at zero temperature, the minimum energy required to break a Cooper pair, denoted E_pair, satisfies the identity

  E_pair = 2|Δ|,

where Δ is the complex order-parameter (gap) amplitude. Small fluctuations of |Δ| about its equilibrium value support an amplitude (Higgs) collective branch which, in the BCS approximation at T = 0 and at zero wave number, produces undamped oscillations whose frequency tends to 2|Δ|/ℏ and whose amplitude decays as a power law t^{-α} with α = 1/2 at the unitary limit.

Address the following:

(a) Does the equality E_pair = 2|Δ| continue to hold at zero temperature in theories that go beyond BCS mean field (for instance theories that include pairing fluctuations or correlations beyond mean field) and/or in laboratory measurements on strongly interacting Fermi gases? Provide a proof, a counterexample, or a precise quantitative correction.

(b) For experiments performed at nonzero temperature in the unitary regime that probe the zero-wave-number oscillations of the order-parameter amplitude, give a theoretical interpretation that accounts simultaneously for: (i) a measured power-law decay exponent α ≈ 1 (rather than the BCS value 1/2 at unitarity); (ii) the possibility that the decay is in fact exponential rather than power-law; and (iii) the absence of any observable softening (reduction) of the oscillation angular frequency as the temperature approaches the superfluid critical temperature T_c. Determine whether such observations are compatible with a Higgs amplitude-mode interpretation and, if not, identify the dominant physical mechanism responsible for the oscillations and their decay.
artifact.category_tag: Strongly interacting Fermi gases / Higgs mode
artifact.status_search_result: Recent theoretical and experimental works (2019–2025) on Higgs oscillations in unitary Fermi superfluids confirm a resonance near 2|Δ| and qualitative agreement with time-dependent BCS theory but do not rigorously establish E_pair = 2|Δ| beyond mean field, and the discrepancies in decay exponent, possible exponential damping, and the lack of frequency softening near T_c remain unresolved. The status is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: Higgs oscillations in a unitary Fermi superfluid
status_evidence.snippet: Amplitude oscillations near 2Δ within the pair-breaking continuum, decay analyzed within time-dependent BCS.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical Higgs-mode predictions are based on BCS-level treatment and yield power-law decays such as t^{-1/2} at unitarity.

status_evidence.title: Generation and decay of Higgs mode in a strongly interacting Fermi gas
status_evidence.snippet: Experimental observation of Higgs-mode oscillations and their decay in a strongly interacting Fermi gas.
status_evidence.claim: Experiments report decay characteristics that are not fully captured by the simplest zero-temperature Higgs picture.

status_evidence.title: Schmid-Higgs Mode in the Presence of Pair-Breaking Interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work studying the amplitude mode with pair-breaking interactions beyond standard BCS.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond-BCS treatments of the amplitude mode are still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: BCS–BEC crossover review
status_evidence.snippet: Pairing fluctuations beyond mean field are essential at finite temperature.
status_evidence.claim: There is no consensus rigorous result establishing E_pair = 2|Δ| beyond BCS at T=0.
